title: HouseVis: datapoints
description: Where the displayed values come from. Every datapoint has its own id, names its source and that source's address, and says how the raw value is converted. Rooms and openings in house.json refer only to the id; the same datapoint may be used several times. Credentials are never stored here but in the device settings.

^(\\$schema|_.*)$.description: Reference to the schema or a comment; ignored.

sources.description: Data sources by name. The name is used in the datapoints; each device sets up the connection (address, sign-in) itself.

type.description: Loxone Miniserver, live values via the WebSocket.

cameras.description: Network cameras by id, shown on a page by a camera component (docs/cameras.md). Addresses only: the sign-in is stored on each device, encrypted (menu "Kameras …").

type.description: reolink: snapshots over its CGI API and the live picture as HTTP-FLV (sub stream; enable HTTP and RTMP under Network > Advanced > Server settings). loxoneIntercom: a Loxone Intercom (gen. 2) through the Miniserver HouseVis is signed in to (TLS only; MJPEG; a Miniserver user's password). snapshot: any camera with a JPEG snapshot address and HTTP Basic sign-in; no live picture.

name.description: Shown in a framed camera component and in the sign-in dialog.

host.description: reolink, snapshot: host name or IPv4 address in the home network, without scheme, port or path.

tls.description: HTTPS with the normal certificate check. Most cameras have a certificate of their own that does not pass it; leave it off in the home network.

channel.description: reolink: the channel on an NVR (or a camera with several lenses); absent: 0.

stream.description: reolink: the stream of the live picture. sub (default): the small "fluent" one every Reolink has, H.264; ext: the "balanced" one some models have; main: full size, often H.265, which plays only with hardware decoding.

path.description: snapshot: path and query of the JPEG snapshot on the camera, e.g. "/cgi-bin/snapshot.cgi?channel=1".

device.description: loxoneIntercom: the intercom's deviceUuid (details of the IntercomV2 control in the structure file).

label.description: Optional description for humans, e.g. the name in Loxone Config.

unit.description: Unit for the display, e.g. "°C", "%", "W"; written after the number when there is no "format".

format.description: How the value is written, in Loxone's printf-like format as the structure file gives it (details.format, or a per-state format such as a Meter's actualFormat): "%.1f°", "%.0f%%", "%.2f kW". Takes precedence over "unit" and "decimals".

as.description: Conversion of the raw value. Short form "number", "boolean", "text" or "color"; without it, "number" applies. "color" parses Loxone colors such as "hsv(30,80,100)" and "temp(80,2700)" (brightness, Kelvin).

loxoneAddress.description: A state of a Loxone control. The UUID is that of the control (uuidAction in LoxApp3.json or the UUID in Loxone Config); the state is the name from its "states", e.g. "tempActual" on the room controller or "active" on the presence detector.

control.description: UUID of the control or subcontrol (then with a suffix such as "/AI1").

scale.description: Factor applied to the raw value (default 1).

equals.description: True if the raw value equals exactly this value.

notEquals.description: True if the raw value does not equal this value, e.g. "[778]" (light mood "Off").

threshold.description: True if the raw value is greater (default 0).

invert.description: Invert the result, e.g. for contacts that report "1" when closed.

asClimateDemand.description: true while a room controller (IRoomControllerV2) demands heating or cooling. The address is the climate controller's state "controls" (a list of the room controllers with their demand: -1 cooling, 0 none, 1 heating); "control" picks the room controller by its UUID. Unlike a valve, it tells heating and cooling apart.

asWindowMonitor.description: One window or door of a "Fenster- und Türüberwachung" (WindowMonitor), for contacts that are not enabled for the user interface themselves. The address is the block's state "windowStates" (the windows' states separated by commas, in the order of the block's details.windows; each a bitmask: 1 closed, 2 tilted, 4 open, 8 locked, 16 unlocked); "window" picks the window, "state" the bit. true while that bit is set; no value while the sensor is offline.

window.description: Position of the window in the block's details.windows, from 0 (the Loxone inventory lists them as "windows").

state.description: The bit that makes the value true: "open" for an opening's "open", "tilted" for its "tilted".

name.description: The window's name in the block. Optional; the Loxone inventory reports a datapoint whose window has another name now, e.g. because a window was added to the block and the positions shifted.
